The '''Ajtai–Komlós–Tusnády theorem''' (also known as the '''AKT optimal matching theorem''') is a result in [[probabilistic combinatorics]]. Given two random, distinct sets of points <math>X=(X_1,\dots,X_k)</math> and <math>Y=(Y_1,\dots,Y_k)</math> in the [[unit square]] <math>[0,1]^2</math>, the theorem gives [[upper and lower bounds]] for the minimal total distance needed to match the points in one set to those in the other.

The theorem was proven in 1984 by the [[Hungarians|Hungarian]] mathematicians [[Miklós Ajtai]], [[János Komlós (mathematician)|János Komlós]], and [[Gábor Tusnády]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ajtai |first1=M. |last2=Komlós |first2=János |last3=Tusnády |first3=G. |title=On optimal matchings |journal=Combinatorica |volume=4 |pages=259–264 |year=1984 |doi=10.1007/BF02579135}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bobkov |first1=Sergey |last2=Ledoux |first2=Michel |title=A simple Fourier analytic proof of the AKT optimal matching theorem |year=2019|journal=[[Annals of Applied Probability]] |volume=31 |number=6|doi=10.1214/20-AAP1656|arxiv=1909.06193 }}</ref>

== Statement ==
Let <math>(X_1,\dots,X_k)</math> and <math>(Y_1,\dots,Y_k)</math> be two independent random vectors, uniformly distributed over <math>[0,1]^2</math> (i.e., <math>X_i \in [0,1]^2</math>). Let <math>S_n</math> denote the [[symmetric group]], and <math>|\cdot|</math> the [[Euclidean norm]] on <math>\R^2</math>.

Then,
:<math>\mathbb{P}\left(C_1\sqrt{n \log n}<\inf\limits_{\sigma \in S_n}\sum\limits_{k=1}^n|X_k-Y_{\sigma(k)}| <C_2\sqrt{n \log n}\right)=1-o(1),</math>
where <math>C_1, C_2</math> are real constants.

=== Remarks ===
* The notation <math>o(1)</math> means
::<math>f(n)\in o(1)\iff \lim\limits_{n\to\infty}f(n)= 0.</math> &nbsp; &nbsp; see [[Landau notation]].
* The theorem implies that
::<math>\inf\limits_{\sigma \in S_n}\frac{1}{n}\sum\limits_{k=1}^n|X_k-Y_{\sigma(k)}| \sim \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}</math>
:with high probability.
